_clinical_sign_off.note: Tier values and the Suspected Stroke symptom list in this file are drafted by engineering from publicly described Kerala-protocol-style triage categories and FAST stroke screening, NOT by a clinician. They must be read against the source Kerala Health Services triage protocol by a qualified clinical owner before any real (non-synthetic) use. See docs/architecture.md section 5, 'Open item for the clinical owner', and loop L27 (protocol change sign-off must block merge without a recorded reviewer).

conditions.name: Chest Pain
conditions.notes: Escalates to C1 (emergency referral) when a cardiac warning sign is present alongside chest pain.

conditions.name: Breathing Difficulty
conditions.notes: Cyanosis, inability to complete a sentence, or stridor escalates to C1 emergency referral.

conditions.name: High Fever
conditions.notes: Meningitis-pattern or seizure-with-fever warning signs escalate to urgent (C2) referral rather than routine PHC follow-up.

conditions.name: Trauma / Injury
conditions.notes: Uncontrolled bleeding, loss of consciousness, or suspected spinal injury escalates directly to C1.

conditions.name: Suspected Stroke (FAST)
conditions.notes: DRAFT, NOT CLINICALLY SIGNED OFF. Modeled on the FAST stroke screen: any single required symptom (Face, Arm, Speech) is sufficient to suspect stroke and must resolve to C1, a mandatory referral trigger, per architecture.md T1/T2. Time-to-treatment is critical; this condition is also the trigger for the acuity floor in kerala_protocol_mcp.py's apply_acuity_floor.
